en.name: Mary Magdalene
en.summary: Devoted follower of Jesus, present at the crucifixion, who became the first witness of the Resurrection and was sent to announce it to the apostles.
en.body: Mary of Magdala is described in the Gospels as a woman Jesus healed of seven demons, after which she became one of his most devoted followers, part of a group of women who supported his ministry and who remained present at the crucifixion even as most of the male disciples fled. She is recorded as one of the women who went to anoint Christ's body on Easter morning, discovering the empty tomb, and in John's Gospel she alone encounters the risen Christ directly, initially mistaking him for a gardener before recognizing him when he speaks her name; he then instructs her to go and tell the apostles, earning her the ancient title "Apostle to the Apostles." A long-standing Western tradition, now generally regarded by scholars as a conflation of separate New Testament women, once identified her with the penitent sinner who anointed Jesus's feet, a conflation the Church has since clarified is not supported by the biblical text. She remains one of the most significant and closely studied women in the Gospels, central to the Resurrection narrative itself.
